messages.content: Please fix this: She don't like maths but she study it every day.

She doesn't like maths, but she studies it every day.
Why: subject-verb agreement ("she don't" -> "doesn't"); subject-verb agreement ("she study" -> "studies"); punctuation (missing comma -> comma before "but").
Can you correct my sentence? My brother is more taller than me.

My brother is taller than me.
Why: comparative ("more taller" -> "taller").
Is this right? We reached to Jaipur at night and was very tired.

We reached Jaipur at night and were very tired.
Why: extra word ("reached to" -> "reached"); subject-verb agreement ("and was" -> "and were").
Fix the mistakes please: I am wanting a cup of chai and two samosa.

I want a cup of chai and two samosas.
Why: verb form ("am wanting" -> "want"); plural ("two samosa" -> "two samosas").
Rohan and me went to the park yesterday. Correct?

Rohan and I went to the park yesterday.
Why: pronoun ("Rohan and me" -> "Rohan and I").
Check my email line: I have sent the report yesterday to my manager.

I sent the report to my manager yesterday.
Why: past tense ("have sent" -> "sent"); word order ("yesterday to my manager" -> "to my manager yesterday").
Could you make this sentence correct? Everyday I drink eight glass of water.

Every day I drink eight glasses of water.
Why: spelling ("Everyday" -> "Every day"); plural ("eight glass" -> "eight glasses").
What is wrong here: Priya has been playing badminton since three years.

Priya has been playing badminton for three years.
Why: preposition ("since three years" -> "for three years").
Help me fix this line. He borrowed me five hundred rupees last week.

He lent me five hundred rupees last week.
Why: word choice ("borrowed me" -> "lent me").
Correct my grammar: There is many birds on the neem tree in morning.

There are many birds on the neem tree in the morning.
Why: subject-verb agreement ("There is many birds" -> "There are"); article ("in morning" -> "in the morning").
During Diwali we decorates our house with diyas and light. Is the grammar okay?

During Diwali, we decorate our house with diyas and lights.
Why: subject-verb agreement ("we decorates" -> "decorate"); plural ("light" -> "lights"); punctuation (missing comma -> "Diwali,").
I want to say this correctly: Anna has read that book two times before she gave it to me.

Anna had read that book twice before she gave it to me.
Why: perfect tense ("has read" -> "had read"); word choice ("two times" -> "twice").
Make this right: I am very boring today because there is nothing to do.

I am very bored today because there is nothing to do.
Why: word choice ("boring" -> "bored").
Spot the errors: If I will finish my homework early, I will watch a movie.

If I finish my homework early, I will watch a movie.
Why: future tense ("If I will finish" -> "If I finish").
Our train was late by two hours, so we have missed the bus. Please correct.

Our train was two hours late, so we missed the bus.
Why: word order ("late by two hours" -> "two hours late"); past tense ("have missed" -> "missed").
Grammar check needed: My grandmother she lives with us since 2015.

My grandmother has lived with us since 2015.
Why: extra word ("grandmother she" -> "grandmother"); perfect tense ("lives since" -> "has lived since").
Does this sound right? Meera is working in a bank and she is knowing three languages.

Meera works in a bank, and she knows three languages.
Why: verb form ("is knowing" -> "knows"); present tense ("is working" -> "works"); punctuation (missing comma -> comma before "and").
Could you fix it? Can you give me an advice on cooking rice without it sticking?

Can you give me some advice on cooking rice so that it does not stick?
Why: article ("an advice" -> "some advice"); verb form ("it sticking" -> "so that it does not stick").
Edit this for me: Each of the girls have brought their own tiffin.

Each of the girls has brought her own tiffin.
Why: subject-verb agreement ("Each have" -> "has"); pronoun ("their" -> "her").
Tell me the correct form: The team are playing good this season, they won five matches.

The team is playing well this season. They have won five matches.
Why: word choice ("good" -> "well"); subject-verb agreement ("are" -> "is"); punctuation ("," -> "."); perfect tense ("won" -> "have won").
